basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 24.' and it opens '(Vers. 24.) Et ejecit Adam, et habitare fecit contra paradisum voluptatis. Et statuit'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 24.) Et ejecit Adam, et habitare fecit contra paradisum voluptatis. Et statuit Cherubim et flammeam romphaeam, quae vertitur ad custodiendam viam ligni vitae. Alius multo sensus est in Hebraeo quam hic intelligitur. Ait enim: Et ejecit Adam, haud dubium quin Dominus: Et habitare fecit ante paradisum voluptatis Cherubim, et flammeum gladium, qui verteretur, et custodiret viam ligni vitae. Non quod ipsum Adam, quem ejecerat Deus, habitare fecerit contra paradisum voluptatis; sed quod illo ejecto ante fores paradisi Cherubim, et flammeum gladium posuerit ad custodiendum paradisi vestibulum, ne quis posset intrare.
